title: What your things say
translation: When the pictures or the writing on a folding screen or a sliding door are done in a clumsy hand, it's not so much that they look ugly. It makes you think less of the owner of the house.

In general, the things people own can make you think less of them. I don't mean you have to own only the best. I mean things that have been made graceless and ugly so they won't get damaged, or loaded with pointless extras so they look unusual, all fussy and overdone.
Things should look a little old-fashioned, not showy, not expensive, and simply be good in themselves.
original: {屏風|びやうぶ}{障子|しやうじ}などの{絵|ゑ}も{文字|もじ}も、かたくななる{筆様|ふでやう}して{書|か}きたるが、{見|み}にくきよりも、{宿|やど}の{主人|あるじ}の{拙|つたな}く{覚|おぼ}ゆるなり。
{大|おほ}かた{持|も}てる{調度|てうど}にても、{心|こころ}おとりせらるる{事|こと}はありぬべし。
さのみよき{物|もの}を{持|も}つべしとにもあらず、{損|そん}ぜざらむためとて、{品|しな}なく{見|み}にくきさまに{為|し}なし、{珍|めづら}しからむとて、{用|よう}なき{事|こと}どもしそへ、{煩|わづら}はしく{好|この}みなせるをいふなり。
{古|ふる}めかしきやうにて、いたくことごとしからず、{費|つひえ}もなくて、{物|もの}がらのよきがよきなり。
literal: Pictures and writing on folding screens, sliding panels and the like, written in a boorish brush style: rather than their being ugly to look at, the master of the house seems inept.
In general, even with the furnishings one owns, there are surely cases where one is thought less of.

It is not that one should own only such good things; I mean making things graceless and ugly so that they will not be damaged, adding useless things so that they will be unusual, and fussily having them made to one's taste.
Looking old-fashioned, not very showy, without expense, with good quality in the thing itself: that is good.

notes.text: {屏風|びやうぶ}: a folding screen. {障子|しやうじ}: in Kenkō's time, any sliding panel between rooms, often covered with heavy paper and painted or written on. Modern shōji, with thin translucent paper, are only one kind.
かたくな: 'clumsy, without taste' (compare section 79). {筆様|ふでやう}: the style of the brushwork, in pictures and calligraphy alike.

notes.quote: 宿の主人の拙く覚ゆるなり
notes.text: The point: the owner chose this and hung it in his house, so it shows his taste, not only the painter's.
{心|こころ}おとり: 'thinking less of someone than before', the same word as in section 1. らる here is spontaneous: 'one can't help thinking less'.
'So that it will not be damaged': things made sturdy and ugly, with no care for how they look.
ことごとし: 'showy, overdone'. {費|つひえ}: 'expense'.

notes.quote: 物がらのよきがよきなり
notes.text: {物|もの}がら: 'the quality of the thing itself'. The sentence is built on よし twice: 'good quality is what is good'.
